label: ER status reverse coding
text: PITFALL: ER_STATUS in data_clinical_patient.txt is reverse-coded (header says 1 = negative, 0 = positive); assuming 1 = positive flips the direction of the conclusion. CHECK: read the # description line and cross-tabulate ER_STATUS against ER_PERCENT_POSITIVE (negatives should have 0 percent). IF FOUND: recode explicitly to ER_pos = (ER_STATUS == 0) and resolve any status/percent disagreements before comparing groups. SOURCE: column metadata in the data file (web search unavailable).

label: Multiple samples per patient
text: PITFALL: the proliferation score is at sample level and patients may have several samples (primary and metastasis), so naive sample-level tests pseudoreplicate and over-weight some patients. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID and tabulate SAMPLE_TYPE. IF FOUND: use one sample per patient (preferably the primary tumour) or aggregate per patient, or use a mixed model with patient random effect; also check whether results differ for primary-only. SOURCE: standard clustered-data guidance (web search unavailable).

label: Batch confounding
text: PITFALL: PROCESSING_BATCH may be confounded with ER group, creating or masking a proliferation difference through batch effects. CHECK: cross-tabulate batch by ER status and compare proliferation score distributions by batch. IF FOUND: adjust for batch (regression covariate or stratified/within-batch comparison); if batch is fully confounded with ER, the comparison may be unresolvable. SOURCE: Leek et al. 2010 Nat Rev Genet batch effects (from knowledge; web search unavailable).

label: site confounding of lab values
text: PITFALL: Serum albumin was measured by each hospital site's own lab (SITE column), and between-lab calibration/assay offsets (e.g. bromocresol green vs purple) combined with site differences in TP53-mutant fraction can create or mask a pooled difference (Simpson's paradox). CHECK: tabulate TP53_STATUS by SITE and mean SERUM_ALBUMIN by SITE; compare the pooled mutant-vs-wildtype difference with within-site differences. IF FOUND: base the conclusion on a site-stratified/adjusted estimate (albumin ~ TP53 + SITE, or a within-site comparison / site-centred albumin), not the pooled t-test. SOURCE: general methods knowledge (search tool unavailable); cf. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simpson%27s_paradox

label: Tumour purity confounding
text: PITFALL: expression signature scores depend on TUMOR_PURITY, and purity can differ between ER groups, confounding the comparison. CHECK: correlate proliferation score with purity and compare purity across ER groups. IF FOUND: adjust for purity in a regression (proliferation ~ ER + purity + batch) and report both crude and adjusted estimates. SOURCE: Aran et al. 2015 Nat Commun on tumour purity (from knowledge; web search unavailable).

label: TP53 status vs VAF discordance
text: PITFALL: TP53_STATUS can disagree with TP53_VAF (header rows already show status=1 with VAF=0.000), so the exposure may be misclassified. CHECK: cross-tab TP53_STATUS against TP53_VAF>0; count mutant with VAF=0 and wild-type with VAF>0, and see whether these cluster by SITE or batch. IF FOUND: run the analysis both with status as given and with a corrected/excluded discordant set; report whether the conclusion is robust, and prefer the internally consistent definition. SOURCE: general methods knowledge (search tool unavailable)

label: smoking coding inverted
text: PITFALL: SMOKING_HISTORY in data_clinical_supplement.txt is coded 1 = never smoker, 0 = current or former smoker (inverse of the usual convention), so a naive 'smoker=1' reading flips the direction of the effect. CHECK: read the '#' description line; cross-tab SMOKING_HISTORY against PACK_YEARS (never smokers should have PACK_YEARS 0). IF FOUND: recode explicitly to ever_smoker = (SMOKING_HISTORY==0) before any comparison and state the direction as ever minus never. SOURCE: data dictionary in data_clinical_supplement.txt header (web search unavailable).

label: stromal score vs purity
text: PITFALL: Stromal score is mechanically anti-correlated with tumour purity (stroma fraction ~ 1 - purity), so a group difference in stromal score may just reflect different purity of sampled tissue. CHECK: correlate STROMAL_SCORE with TUMOR_PURITY and compare purity between ever and never smokers. IF FOUND: report the unadjusted comparison as primary for the hypothesis as stated, but also fit STROMAL_SCORE ~ ever_smoker + TUMOR_PURITY and note whether the direction changes. SOURCE: Yoshihara et al. 2013 Nat Commun (ESTIMATE), https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms3612

label: Direction of effect
text: PITFALL: a one-sided hypothesis (ER-positive higher) can be wrongly labelled Not verifiable or True when the data show a significant difference in the opposite direction; established breast cancer biology is that ER-negative tumours are usually MORE proliferative. CHECK: report the direction and effect size (mean/median difference with CI) not just a p-value. IF FOUND: if ER-negative is clearly higher, the correct label is False, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: general breast cancer biology knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: unit of analysis / duplicates
text: PITFALL: Duplicated patients or multiple samples per patient (sample table) can be double-counted if albumin is joined at sample level. CHECK: confirm PATIENT_ID is unique in data_clinical_patient.txt and count samples per patient before any merge. IF FOUND: analyse at one row per patient (albumin and TP53 are patient-level columns); deduplicate. SOURCE: general methods knowledge (search tool unavailable)

label: processing batch confounding
text: PITFALL: Expression-derived scores like STROMAL_SCORE shift between laboratory processing batches; if smokers are unevenly spread across PROCESSING_BATCH the batch effect can create or hide a difference. CHECK: tabulate ever_smoker by PROCESSING_BATCH and compare STROMAL_SCORE means per batch. IF FOUND: compare within batch (stratified test or regression with batch fixed effects) and check the direction is consistent across batches. SOURCE: Leek et al. 2010 Nat Rev Genet, https://www.nature.com/articles/nrg2825

label: Missing data and join integrity
text: PITFALL: missing values, sentinel codes or outliers in PROLIFERATION_SCORE, ER_STATUS or ER_PERCENT_POSITIVE, and samples whose PATIENT_ID does not join to the patient table, can silently bias the comparison. CHECK: count NA/blank/out-of-range values and unmatched IDs after the merge; inspect the score distribution for skew. IF FOUND: exclude or document them and use a rank-based test (Mann-Whitney) or robust regression alongside the t-test. SOURCE: general data-quality practice (web search unavailable).

label: albumin units/outliers
text: PITFALL: Implausible or sentinel albumin values (e.g. 0, negative, >6 g/dL, values in g/L instead of g/dL at one site, 999 codes) can drive a mean difference. CHECK: summarise SERUM_ALBUMIN range per SITE; flag values outside ~1.5-6 g/dL or a site whose scale is ~10x others. IF FOUND: convert units or exclude invalid values, then use a robust test (Mann-Whitney, or regression with site) and check the result is unchanged. SOURCE: general methods knowledge (search tool unavailable)

label: multiple samples per patient
text: PITFALL: data_clinical_sample.txt may hold several samples per patient (primary and metastasis), while smoking is per patient; treating samples as independent inflates n and mixes tissue types whose stroma differs. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID and the SAMPLE_TYPE distribution by smoking group. IF FOUND: use one sample per patient (e.g. primary only) or average per patient, and/or adjust for SAMPLE_TYPE; report sensitivity. SOURCE: standard clustered-data guidance, e.g. Galbraith et al. 2010 https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.c2073 (not fetched; search unavailable).

label: Site and sample type stratification
text: PITFALL: SITE (hospital) may differ in ER mix and in assay handling, and metastases vs primaries differ in proliferation, so a crude difference may be Simpson-type confounding. CHECK: compare the ER effect within SITE and within SAMPLE_TYPE strata. IF FOUND: report stratified or covariate-adjusted estimates and prefer them if the crude direction reverses. SOURCE: standard confounding guidance (web search unavailable).

label: clinical confounders of albumin
text: PITFALL: Albumin falls with poor performance status, cachexia (low BMI), age and kidney dysfunction, so a crude TP53 difference may reflect sicker patients rather than TP53 itself, though these may be mediators. CHECK: compare ECOG_PS, BMI, AGE, SERUM_CREATININE between TP53 groups and fit albumin ~ TP53 + SITE + AGE (+ ECOG, BMI as sensitivity). IF FOUND: report crude and adjusted estimates; do not over-adjust for mediators, but treat site as the key confounder. SOURCE: general methods knowledge (search tool unavailable)

label: table merge losses
text: PITFALL: Joining patient, sample and supplement tables can silently drop or duplicate rows (ID mismatches, whitespace/case differences, patients missing smoking data). CHECK: report row counts before/after each merge on PATIENT_ID and the number with missing SMOKING_HISTORY or STROMAL_SCORE. IF FOUND: fix ID formats, do not impute smoking status, and state the analysed n. SOURCE: general data-handling practice (search unavailable).

label: decision rule direction/CI
text: PITFALL: A non-significant difference is not evidence of no difference, and a significant difference in the opposite direction is what supports 'False'. CHECK: report the direction, effect size in g/dL with 95% CI and p-value for the site-adjusted estimate. IF FOUND: label True only if the adjusted mutant-minus-wildtype is negative and significant; False if clearly null with tight CI or significantly positive; avoid calling 'Not verifiable' since both variables exist. SOURCE: general statistical guidance (search tool unavailable)

label: site confounding
text: PITFALL: Hospital SITE can confound both smoking prevalence and the assay/tissue handling that drives stromal score (site differences are a classic Simpson's paradox source). CHECK: tabulate ever_smoker by SITE and STROMAL_SCORE by SITE. IF FOUND: stratify by SITE or include it as a covariate and check the smoking effect keeps its sign within sites. SOURCE: general confounding guidance (search unavailable).

label: TP53 coding inverted
text: PITFALL: TP53_STATUS is coded backwards from intuition (1 = wild type, 0 = mutant), so reading 1 as mutant flips the direction of the comparison. CHECK: confirm against the column description and TP53_VAF (must be 0 when TP53_STATUS=1). IF FOUND: recode to an explicit label such as 'WT'/'MUT' before any test, and state the direction (WT minus MUT). SOURCE: data_clinical_patient.txt header (web search unavailable).

label: outliers and sentinel values
text: PITFALL: Stromal scores can be skewed, contain outliers or sentinel values (e.g. -999, NA strings), so a t-test on means can be driven by a few points. CHECK: inspect distribution, min/max and any sentinel codes of STROMAL_SCORE per group. IF FOUND: remove sentinels as missing and use a Mann-Whitney test alongside the t-test; report effect size with CI. SOURCE: general statistical practice (search unavailable).

label: label decision rule
text: PITFALL: Deciding 'False' vs 'Not verifiable': with smoking and stromal score both present the hypothesis IS testable, so a clear opposite-direction difference means False, while a null/non-significant result is not support. CHECK: compute effect direction, CI and p for ever vs never. IF FOUND: significant ever>never -> True; significant ever<never -> False; reserve Not verifiable for missing variables only. SOURCE: task label definitions.

label: Purity confounding
text: PITFALL: tumour purity confounds expression-based immune infiltration scores, because a sample with low tumour fraction has more non-tumour (immune/stromal) cells, and purity may differ between TP53 groups. CHECK: correlate TUMOR_PURITY with IMMUNE_INFILTRATION_SCORE and compare purity between TP53 WT and mutant. IF FOUND: base the conclusion on a regression of the immune score on TP53 status plus purity (and batch/site), not on a raw two-group test; report both and say if the sign flips. SOURCE: Aran, Sirota & Butte 2015 Nat Commun 'Systematic pan-cancer analysis of tumour purity' https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms9971 (not fetched; search tool down).

label: Batch confounding
text: PITFALL: the expression assay was run in processing batches, and batch effects can shift signature scores; if TP53 groups are spread unevenly across batches this creates or hides a difference. CHECK: cross-tab PROCESSING_BATCH by TP53 status, and look at mean immune score by batch. IF FOUND: add batch as a covariate (fixed effect) or stratify by batch; do not trust a pooled unadjusted test. SOURCE: Leek et al. 2010 Nat Rev Genet 'Tackling the widespread and critical impact of batch effects' https://www.nature.com/articles/nrg2825 (not fetched).

label: Repeated samples per patient
text: PITFALL: the sample table can hold more than one sample per patient (primary and metastasis), so a sample-level test counts patients twice, and metastases can have different immune contexture from primaries. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID and tabulate SAMPLE_TYPE. IF FOUND: run the main analysis on one sample per patient (e.g. primary only), or use a mixed model with a patient random effect; check whether results agree. SOURCE: Lazic 2010 BMC Neurosci on pseudoreplication https://bmcneurosci.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1471-2202-11-5 (not fetched).

label: Prior chemo coding is inverted
text: PITFALL: The PRIOR_CHEMOTHERAPY column in data_clinical_patient.txt is reverse-coded per its own header (1 = not received, 0 = received); reading 1 as 'received' flips the direction of the comparison and the label. CHECK: cross-tabulate PRIOR_CHEMOTHERAPY against PRIOR_CHEMO_CYCLES (cycles should be >0 when code=0 and 0 when code=1) and count discordant rows. IF FOUND: recode to an explicit received/not-received variable before any test, and treat discordant rows as data errors to report/exclude in a sensitivity analysis. SOURCE: column descriptions in /planted-data/data_clinical_patient.txt

label: Join and missingness
text: PITFALL: TP53 status lives in the patient table and the immune score in the sample table; a bad join (mismatched IDs, duplicates, unmatched rows silently dropped) changes the n and the groups. CHECK: report row counts before and after merging on PATIENT_ID, and list any IDs with no match or with missing TP53/immune values. IF FOUND: fix the join and handle missing data explicitly (complete-case, stating how many were dropped per group). SOURCE: general data-handling practice (search tool down).

label: Site lab calibration/units confound creatinine
text: PITFALL: Serum creatinine was measured by each enrolling hospital (SITE 'ran the blood tests'); labs differ in calibration (Jaffe vs enzymatic, IDMS traceability) and sometimes report umol/L instead of mg/dL (factor 88.4), so a pooled comparison can be driven by site, not chemotherapy. CHECK: summarise creatinine distribution (median, range) by SITE and look for a site with values ~88x larger or shifted; cross-tab SITE by chemo group to see if chemo prevalence differs by site. IF FOUND: convert mis-scaled values to mg/dL (divide by 88.4) and compare chemo groups within site (stratified test, regression with site fixed effects, or van Elteren); report pooled and stratified results and trust the stratified one if they disagree (Simpson's paradox). SOURCE: Myers GL et al., Clin Chem 2006;52:5-18 (creatinine standardization, NKDEP) - not retrieved, search tool down

label: Sex/age/body size confound creatinine
text: PITFALL: Serum creatinine depends strongly on sex (men ~0.2 mg/dL higher, muscle mass), age and body size; if the chemo groups differ in sex mix or age, a raw difference may be confounding. CHECK: compare sex proportions, age and BMI (BMI in data_clinical_supplement.txt) between chemo groups. IF FOUND: adjust via linear regression of creatinine (or log creatinine) on chemo + sex + age (+ site, BMI) and base the conclusion on the adjusted chemo coefficient direction and CI. SOURCE: Levey AS et al., Ann Intern Med 2009;150:604-612 (CKD-EPI, sex/age terms) - not retrieved

label: Direction and effect size
text: PITFALL: the hypothesis is directional (WT lower than mutant); a significant difference in the opposite direction is evidence for False, while a small non-significant difference is not the same as a contradiction. CHECK: report the effect size with a 95% CI (difference in means or medians, Hodges-Lehmann) and the direction, not only a p-value. IF FOUND: True if WT is significantly lower after adjustment; False if WT is clearly higher, or if the adjusted estimate is null with a CI that excludes a meaningful difference; state what was decided and why. SOURCE: Wasserstein & Lazar 2016 ASA statement on p-values https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2016.1154108 (not fetched).

label: Multiple samples per patient (pseudoreplication)
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (pseudoreplication). CHECK: Count samples per PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt and tabulate SAMPLE_TYPE (Primary vs Metastasis); statin use is patient-level. IF FOUND: Do not treat samples as independent: analyse one sample per patient (prefer the primary tumour) or aggregate per patient, or use a mixed model with a patient random effect; check the result holds in primary-only samples. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.2307/1942661 (cited from prior knowledge; research tool was unavailable).

label: Skew, outliers and sentinel values in creatinine
text: PITFALL: Creatinine is right-skewed with possible outliers or impossible values (<=0, >15 mg/dL, sentinel codes like 999), and a t-test on raw values can be dominated by a few points. CHECK: inspect min/max, histogram, missing and sentinel values of SERUM_CREATININE per group. IF FOUND: set impossible/sentinel values to missing, use Mann-Whitney / log-transformed regression, and confirm the direction matches the median difference. SOURCE: general clinical-lab data-cleaning practice (no source retrieved)

label: Site / Simpson's paradox
text: PITFALL: enrolment site (SITE) can differ in case-mix and in its TP53 distribution, which gives a Simpson's-paradox-style reversal when data are pooled. CHECK: compare WT vs mutant immune score within each SITE and within each batch, and look for sign reversals versus the pooled result. IF FOUND: report the stratified or adjusted estimate (site as a covariate) as the primary result. SOURCE: standard confounding/stratification practice (search tool down).

label: Stromal score depends on tumour purity
text: PITFALL: Stromal score depends on tumour purity. CHECK: Correlate STROMAL_SCORE with TUMOR_PURITY and compare purity between statin users and non-users. IF FOUND: ESTIMATE-type stromal scores fall as purity rises. If purity differs by statin group, report the adjusted estimate (regress stromal score on statin + purity) next to the crude one. Purity is a composition measure, so it may be partly a mediator; say how you interpret it. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms3612 (cited from prior knowledge; research tool was unavailable).

label: Unit of analysis: one row per patient
text: PITFALL: data_clinical_sample.txt can contain several samples per patient; merging it onto the patient table before testing duplicates patients and inflates n and significance for a patient-level variable like creatinine. CHECK: count rows per PATIENT_ID in each table and check for duplicate patient rows. IF FOUND: run the creatinine-vs-chemo test on one row per patient (patient table only; dedupe if needed). SOURCE: standard unit-of-analysis guidance (no source retrieved)

label: Distribution and outliers
text: PITFALL: immune signature scores are often skewed or bounded, and outliers can drive a t-test. CHECK: inspect the distribution per group; run a Wilcoxon rank-sum test alongside the t-test, and robust regression or a rank-based model alongside OLS. IF FOUND: base conclusions on the rank-based or robust estimates, and report whether parametric and nonparametric results agree. SOURCE: standard practice (search tool down).

label: ER status reverse-coded
text: PITFALL: ER_STATUS in data_clinical_patient.txt is reverse-coded (column description says 1 = negative, 0 = positive), so treating 1 as ER-positive flips the direction of the comparison. CHECK: read the # description line and cross-tabulate ER_STATUS against ER_PERCENT_POSITIVE (ER-negative should have 0%, positive >0, commonly >=1%). IF FOUND: recode explicitly to ER_POS = (ER_STATUS==0) and report the direction using the recoded variable; flag rows where status and percent disagree. SOURCE: data dictionary in /planted-data; ASCO/CAP ER testing guideline https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.19.02309

label: Direction and labelling rules
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is directional (chemo group LOWER creatinine); a significant two-sided difference in the opposite direction should be labelled False, while a null result is not automatically 'Not verifiable' because the variables exist. CHECK: report the group medians/means, the sign of the adjusted effect and its CI/p-value. IF FOUND: label True only if received-chemo creatinine is significantly lower after recoding and site/sex adjustment; label False if the evidence is null or significantly higher; reserve Not verifiable for missing variables. SOURCE: task label definitions

label: Processing batch confounded with statin group
text: PITFALL: Processing batch confounded with statin group. CHECK: Cross-tabulate PROCESSING_BATCH by STATIN_USE (after joining) and compare STROMAL_SCORE means by batch. IF FOUND: If batches differ in score level and statin prevalence, adjust for batch (fixed effect) or compare within batch; if a batch is nearly all one group, the effect is not identifiable from those batches. Do not use ComBat-style correction that removes the statin signal when design is unbalanced. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/nrg2825 (cited from prior knowledge; research tool was unavailable).

label: Biological prior and muscle-mass confounding
text: PITFALL: Chemotherapy (e.g. cisplatin) is usually nephrotoxic and tends to RAISE creatinine, while cancer cachexia/low muscle mass can lower it; a 'lower creatinine' finding may reflect confounding by muscle mass/performance status rather than a chemo effect. CHECK: check ECOG_PS and BMI by chemo group and whether the chemo effect survives adjustment. IF FOUND: report the adjusted estimate and treat unadjusted-only effects with caution. SOURCE: Perazella MA, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2012 (onconephrology/chemo nephrotoxicity) - not retrieved

label: Site confounding (Simpson's paradox)
text: PITFALL: Site confounding (Simpson's paradox). CHECK: Cross-tabulate SITE by STATIN_USE, compute the statin-vs-non-statin difference within each site, and compare it with the pooled difference. IF FOUND: If within-site differences disagree in sign or size with the pooled difference, base the conclusion on the stratified/adjusted estimate (site fixed effect), not the crude comparison. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1972.10482387 (cited from prior knowledge; research tool was unavailable).

label: multiple samples per patient
text: PITFALL: The sample table can hold several samples per patient (e.g. -T1/-T2, primary plus metastasis), so a naive sample-level test pseudo-replicates patients and inflates significance. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID and SAMPLE_TYPE values after joining to the patient table. IF FOUND: analyse one sample per patient (prefer the primary tumour, since ER is assessed on the primary), or average within patient, or use a mixed model with a patient random effect. SOURCE: Lazic 2010 pseudoreplication https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2202-11-5

label: Site confounding of Hb
text: PITFALL: Site confounding / Simpson's paradox – SITE enrolled patients AND ran the blood tests, so site differences in lab calibration and in radiotherapy rates can create or reverse a pooled haemoglobin difference. CHECK: cross-tab PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY by SITE and compare HEMOGLOBIN mean/median by site; compute the RT effect within each site. IF FOUND: base the conclusion on the site-stratified/adjusted estimate (linear model HEMOGLOBIN ~ PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY + SITE, or within-site standardised values), not the pooled t-test. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simpson%27s_paradox (not fetched; search tool down)

label: Exposure coding inconsistency
text: PITFALL: Exposure coding inconsistency. CHECK: Check that STATIN_USE is only 0/1, that STATIN_DOSE_MG>0 exactly when STATIN_USE=1, and look for missing/sentinel values. IF FOUND: Resolve contradictory records (e.g. user with dose 0) explicitly, report counts, and run a sensitivity analysis; a dose-response check (dose vs score) can strengthen or weaken a causal reading. SOURCE: https://www.equator-network.org/reporting-guidelines/strobe/ (cited from prior knowledge; research tool was unavailable).

label: primary vs metastasis mixing
text: PITFALL: Primary and metastatic samples differ in hypoxia biology and site, and ER status can change between primary and metastasis, so mixing sample types can confound the ER comparison. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_TYPE by ER group and compare hypoxia by sample type. IF FOUND: restrict the main analysis to primary samples and run metastases as a sensitivity analysis, or adjust for sample type. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1093/annonc/mdr525 (ER discordance primary vs metastasis)

label: Join errors between patient and sample tables
text: PITFALL: Join errors between patient and sample tables. CHECK: Check that PATIENT_ID is unique in the patient and supplement tables, count unmatched IDs from each side, and check that the row count after the merge is what you expect. IF FOUND: Remove duplicate patient rows or settle which one is correct before merging. Report how many samples you dropped. Never let a many-to-many join inflate n. SOURCE: https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.merge.html (cited from prior knowledge; research tool was unavailable).

label: Hb unit mixing by site
text: PITFALL: Mixed haemoglobin units across sites (g/dL vs g/L vs mmol/L) make one site's values ~10x or ~0.6x others and dominate any comparison. CHECK: per-SITE distribution of HEMOGLOBIN (min/median/max); g/dL should be ~7-18, g/L ~70-180, mmol/L ~4.5-11. IF FOUND: convert to g/dL (g/L/10; mmol/L*1.611) before analysis, or analyse within site / use rank-based within-site z-scores. SOURCE: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK259/ (not fetched)

label: Outliers, skew and sentinel values in the score
text: PITFALL: Outliers, skew and sentinel values in the score. CHECK: Plot the distribution of STROMAL_SCORE by group and look for impossible values such as -999, NA codes, or values far outside the usual range. IF FOUND: Use a rank-based test (Mann-Whitney) or a robust check next to the t-test. Make the conclusion depend on the direction and size of the effect, not on a single p-value that hinges on a few outliers. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.c2289 (cited from prior knowledge; research tool was unavailable).

label: tumour purity confounding
text: PITFALL: Expression signature scores depend on tumour purity (stromal/immune content dilutes or adds hypoxia genes), and ER-negative tumours often differ in purity and immune infiltration, so a raw ER difference may be a purity effect or may be masked by one. CHECK: correlate HYPOXIA_SCORE with TUMOR_PURITY and compare purity between ER groups. IF FOUND: fit a regression of hypoxia score on ER status adjusted for TUMOR_PURITY and report both crude and adjusted estimates; if they disagree in sign, explain why. SOURCE: Aran et al. 2015 purity confounding https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms9971

label: Directional hypothesis and contradicting evidence
text: PITFALL: Directional hypothesis and contradicting evidence. CHECK: Look at the sign of the adjusted effect as well as its significance. 'Lower in statin users' can be contradicted by a significantly higher score or by a precise null. IF FOUND: Answer 'False' when the variables exist and the adjusted, properly clustered analysis shows no reduction or the opposite direction. Save 'Not verifiable' for when the variables are truly missing. Here STATIN_USE and STROMAL_SCORE both exist. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10654-016-0149-3 (cited from prior knowledge; research tool was unavailable).

label: Sex confounding of Hb
text: PITFALL: Sex confounds haemoglobin (men ~1-2 g/dL higher) and RT exposure may differ by sex. CHECK: cross-tab SEX by PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY and Hb by SEX. IF FOUND: adjust for SEX (and AGE) in the regression or stratify by sex. SOURCE: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240088542 (WHO Hb thresholds; not fetched)

label: processing batch confounding
text: PITFALL: PROCESSING_BATCH (expression assay batch) can shift signature scores, and if ER groups are unevenly spread across batches the ER difference is confounded by batch (a Simpson's-paradox-style reversal is possible). CHECK: cross-tabulate ER group by PROCESSING_BATCH and compare mean hypoxia by batch; look at the ER effect within each batch. IF FOUND: adjust for batch as a fixed effect or stratify (within-batch comparison); do not trust a pooled crude difference. SOURCE: Leek et al. 2010 batch effects https://doi.org/10.1038/nrg2825

label: RT flag vs dose consistency
text: PITFALL: Inconsistent exposure coding – PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY flag may disagree with RT_DOSE_GY (flag 0 with dose>0 or flag 1 with dose 0), or contain missing/strange codes. CHECK: cross-tab PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY vs (RT_DOSE_GY>0); count NA. IF FOUND: report both definitions, run sensitivity analysis; a dose-response (Hb vs dose among treated) strengthens causal reading. SOURCE: https://www.equator-network.org/reporting-guidelines/strobe/ (not fetched)

label: site confounding
text: PITFALL: SITE (enrolling hospital) can be associated with both ER mix and assay or lab handling, which is another source of confounding or clustering. CHECK: tabulate ER by SITE and hypoxia by SITE. IF FOUND: include site as a covariate or stratum, or use cluster-robust standard errors. SOURCE: general multicentre analysis guidance, Kahan & Morris 2012 https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.4485

label: Hb sentinel/outlier values
text: PITFALL: Implausible/sentinel Hb values (0, negative, 999, -1) or outliers drive mean differences. CHECK: range of HEMOGLOBIN, count of values outside 3-25 g/dL after unit harmonisation, NA counts by group. IF FOUND: treat sentinels as missing, report results with and without outliers, use Mann-Whitney / robust regression alongside t-test. SOURCE: https://www.equator-network.org/reporting-guidelines/strobe/ (not fetched)

label: missing/implausible values and join

CHECK: report adjusted effect size with 95% CI and sign. IF FOUND: label True only if adjusted RT effect is negative and CI excludes 0; Not verifiable only if variables are absent. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2016.1154108 (ASA p-value statement; not fetched)

label: site confounding / lab offset
text: PITFALL: Site is both the enrolling hospital and the lab that ran the blood tests, so between-site assay calibration offsets plus unequal smoker proportions across sites can create or reverse a crude cholesterol difference (Simpson's paradox). CHECK: tabulate smoker fraction by SITE and mean TOTAL_CHOLESTEROL by SITE; compare crude smoker-vs-never difference with within-site differences. IF FOUND: base the conclusion on the site-adjusted estimate (OLS cholesterol ~ smoking + C(SITE), or stratified/Mantel-Haenszel-style pooled within-site difference), and report whether direction is consistent across sites. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simpson%27s_paradox (search tool unavailable; general epidemiology guidance)

label: demographic confounders
text: PITFALL: Age, sex and BMI affect cholesterol and differ between smokers and never smokers, so a crude comparison can be confounded. CHECK: compare AGE, SEX, BMI (supplement table, join on PATIENT_ID) by SMOKING_HISTORY. IF FOUND: fit cholesterol ~ smoking + site + age + sex (+ BMI) and check the smoking coefficient sign/CI is stable vs the crude estimate. SOURCE: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK (standard confounding adjustment; search tool unavailable)

label: sentinels and units

CHECK: describe TOTAL_CHOLESTEROL overall and by SITE: min/max, values <50 or >500, count NA, look for a site whose values are ~38x smaller (mmol/L). IF FOUND: set sentinels to missing, convert mmol/L to mg/dL (x38.67), report sensitivity with/without. SOURCE: general data-cleaning guidance (search tool unavailable)

CHECK: crosstab SMOKING_HISTORY values and PACK_YEARS>0. IF FOUND: report inconsistencies, run sensitivity analyses with both definitions; do not silently drop. label: unit of analysis
text: PITFALL: Duplicate patient rows, or joining patient table to sample table (multiple samples per patient) inflates n and fakes significance. CHECK: assert PATIENT_ID unique in data_clinical_patient.txt; do the analysis at patient level only; do not merge in sample table (it has no cholesterol data). IF FOUND: deduplicate to one row per patient. SOURCE: general (search tool unavailable)

label: directional label logic
text: PITFALL: Label logic: the hypothesis is directional (never < ever). A significant difference in the opposite direction, or a crude difference that vanishes/reverses after site adjustment, supports False, not Not verifiable; Not verifiable only applies if variables are absent, and they are present (SMOKING_HISTORY, TOTAL_CHOLESTEROL). CHECK: report adjusted effect sign, 95% CI and p. IF FOUND: a null-ish CI including 0 after proper adjustment with clear absence of effect is evidence against the claim. SOURCE: task instructions

label: robustness
text: PITFALL: Outliers and skew can drive a t-test. CHECK: compare t-test with Mann-Whitney and with robust regression / trimmed means within site. IF FOUND: prefer conclusions consistent across robust methods. SOURCE: general (search tool unavailable)

label: site confounding Simpson
text: PITFALL: Site confounding / Simpson's paradox - the SITE column both enrolled patients and ran the blood tests, so if radiotherapy rates and glucose assay levels both differ by site, the pooled glucose difference between RT groups can be reversed or created by site. CHECK: crosstab PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY by SITE and compare mean/median FASTING_GLUCOSE by SITE; then compare RT groups within each site. IF FOUND: base the conclusion on the site-adjusted estimate (stratified within-site comparison, regression glucose ~ RT + SITE, or van Elteren/stratified test), not the pooled crude difference. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simpson%27s_paradox (search tool failed; standard reference, not fetched)

label: glucose units by site
text: PITFALL: Between-site lab calibration or unit differences - one site may report glucose in mmol/L (values ~3-15) instead of mg/dL (~60-300), or have a systematic offset, which distorts pooled comparisons. CHECK: plot/describe FASTING_GLUCOSE (and creatinine, calcium) distributions per SITE; look for a site with values ~18x lower or clearly shifted. IF FOUND: convert mmol/L to mg/dL (x18.016) for that site, or within-site standardise (z-score) / adjust for site before comparing RT groups. SOURCE: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK248/ (search tool failed; not fetched)

label: sentinel values

CHECK: min/max and value counts of FASTING_GLUCOSE; flag glucose <20 or >1000 mg/dL, NA strings. IF FOUND: set sentinels to missing and report how many were excluded per RT group. SOURCE: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK248/ (search tool failed; not fetched)

Reading 1 as 'had chemo' flips the direction of the result and the label. CHECK: Read the # description line and cross-tabulate PRIOR_CHEMOTHERAPY against PRIOR_CHEMO_CYCLES. Cycles should be 0 exactly when the code is 1. IF FOUND: Recode to an explicit variable such as chemo_received = (PRIOR_CHEMOTHERAPY==0) before any comparison. label: RT coding consistency

CHECK: crosstab PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY vs (RT_DOSE_GY>0) and list unique codes. IF FOUND: report inconsistency, run sensitivity analysis defining exposure by flag and by dose; do not silently drop. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_bias_(epidemiology) (search tool failed; not fetched)

label: Multiple samples per patient
text: PITFALL: The sample table can hold several samples per patient (primary and metastasis). If the immune score is merged onto patient-level chemo status and every sample is treated as independent, patients get duplicated and p-values come out too small. CHECK: Count samples per PATIENT_ID and SAMPLE_TYPE values. Check that merges are one-to-one or many-to-one, and look for patients missing from either table. IF FOUND: Use one sample per patient (e.g. the primary, or the patient mean), or a mixed model with a patient random effect. Report the result both ways. SOURCE: Lazic 2010, BMC Neurosci 11:5 (pseudoreplication); web search unavailable.

label: patient-level analysis
text: PITFALL: Wrong unit of analysis - sample table has multiple samples per patient; merging glucose onto samples duplicates patients and inflates n / weights. Also duplicate PATIENT_ID rows in patient table. CHECK: count unique PATIENT_ID vs rows in each table. IF FOUND: analyse glucose at patient level only (patient table), deduplicate, never use sample-level rows. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudoreplication (search tool failed; not fetched)

label: Sample type confounding
text: PITFALL: Sample type (primary vs metastasis) can confound the chemo comparison. Metastases and post-treatment samples differ in immune infiltration, and pretreated patients more often contribute metastatic samples. CHECK: Cross-tabulate chemo status by SAMPLE_TYPE and compare immune scores by SAMPLE_TYPE. IF FOUND: Stratify by sample type or adjust for it in a regression. Check that the chemo effect keeps its direction within each stratum (Simpson's paradox). SOURCE: general confounding guidance, e.g. Hernan & Robins, Causal Inference: What If (web search unavailable).

label: skew outliers
text: PITFALL: Fasting glucose is right-skewed with outliers (undiagnosed diabetes, steroid use), so a t-test on means can be driven by a few extreme values. CHECK: compare means and medians per group, look at skewness and extreme values. IF FOUND: use Mann-Whitney / log-transformed or robust regression and confirm direction agrees with the mean-based test. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mann%E2%80%93Whitney_U_test (search tool failed; not fetched)

label: Processing batch confounding
text: PITFALL: Expression-based immune scores depend on processing batch. If batch is unbalanced across chemo groups, a batch artefact can produce or hide a group difference. CHECK: Cross-tabulate PROCESSING_BATCH by chemo status and compare the distribution of IMMUNE_INFILTRATION_SCORE by batch (means and boxplots). IF FOUND: Include batch as a covariate or stratum, or compare within batch. Do not batch-correct in a way that removes the chemo signal when batch and chemo are confounded. SOURCE: Leek et al. 2010, Nat Rev Genet 11:733 (batch effects); web search unavailable.

label: BMI age confounding
text: PITFALL: Other confounders of glucose (BMI, AGE in supplement/patient tables) may differ between RT groups, producing a crude difference not due to RT. CHECK: compare BMI and AGE by RT group; fit glucose ~ RT + SITE + AGE + BMI after joining supplement on PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: rely on adjusted estimate; label False only if the adjusted direction contradicts (no-RT lower or significantly opposite), Not verifiable is wrong since variables exist. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confounding (search tool failed; not fetched)

label: Tumour purity confounding
text: PITFALL: Immune and stromal signature scores are tied to tumour purity: low-purity samples have higher immune scores (ESTIMATE). A purity difference between chemo groups can therefore look like an immune difference. CHECK: Correlate IMMUNE_INFILTRATION_SCORE with TUMOR_PURITY and compare purity across chemo groups. IF FOUND: Report the unadjusted comparison and a purity-adjusted regression (immune ~ chemo + purity), and state whether the conclusion changes. SOURCE: Yoshihara et al. 2013, Nat Commun 4:2612 (ESTIMATE); Aran et al. 2015, Nat Commun 6:8971; web search unavailable.

label: label choice
text: PITFALL: Treating a non-significant difference as 'Not verifiable'. Not verifiable is only for missing variables; here PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY and FASTING_GLUCOSE exist, so the label must be True or False based on the direction and strength of the (properly adjusted) evidence. CHECK: confirm both variables exist and are usable after cleaning. IF FOUND: choose True if adjusted no-RT glucose is credibly higher, otherwise False. SOURCE: task label definitions

label: Site confounding
text: PITFALL: Hospital site can differ in both chemo practice and assay handling, which confounds the comparison. Lab variables such as glucose, haemoglobin and creatinine are distractors for this hypothesis. CHECK: Cross-tabulate SITE by chemo status and compare immune scores by SITE. IF FOUND: Adjust for or stratify by site. Do not add unrelated lab variables, which only add noise. SOURCE: general confounding guidance (web search unavailable).

label: Direction and decision rule
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is one-directional: no-chemo patients score higher. A significant difference in the opposite direction means False. No meaningful difference with an adequate sample size is not support, and the variables do exist, so Not verifiable is wrong in that case. CHECK: Report group means or medians, the effect size with a CI, and a Welch t-test or Mann-Whitney test, labelling which group is which after recoding. Check for outliers and missing or non-numeric values. IF FOUND: Base the label on the direction and the CI. Use a nonparametric test if scores are skewed or have outliers. SOURCE: standard statistical practice (web search unavailable).

label: Batch confounding
text: PITFALL: Expression-derived scores such as IFNG_SIGNATURE_SCORE can shift by PROCESSING_BATCH; if ER groups are unevenly spread across batches, a batch shift looks like an ER effect or hides one, and it can even reverse the sign (Simpson's paradox). IF FOUND: Make the batch-adjusted or within-batch-stratified estimate the primary result; if batch and ER are almost fully confounded, say the effect cannot be separated. SOURCE: Leek et al., Nat Rev Genet 2010 (https://doi.org/10.1038/nrg2825).

label: Tumour purity confounding
text: PITFALL: Bulk-expression immune/IFN-gamma scores fall mechanically as tumour purity rises (fewer immune cells in the sample), so a difference in TUMOR_PURITY between ER groups can create or mask an IFNG difference. CHECK: Correlate IFNG score with TUMOR_PURITY; compare purity across ER groups; fit IFNG ~ ER + purity (and + batch). IF FOUND: Report the purity-adjusted ER effect alongside the raw effect and base the label on whether the direction is consistent. CHECK: Compute the group means/medians and the effect direction from the data itself, using the correct coding. IF FOUND: Label strictly by the data: a significant difference in the opposite direction = False, consistent lower in ER-neg = True; a null result with adequate n leans toward the hypothesis not being supported (False rather than Not verifiable, because the variables exist). SOURCE: Denkert et al., Lancet Oncol 2018, TILs by subtype (https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(17)30904-X).

label: Join and missing data

SOURCE: Little & Rubin, Statistical Analysis with Missing Data (https://doi.org/10.1002/9781119482260).

label: Outliers and test choice
text: PITFALL: Signature scores can be skewed, have outliers or impossible values (e.g. purity >1), so a t-test on raw means can be driven by a few points. SOURCE: Fagerland, BMC Med Res Methodol 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2288-12-78).

reason: Site is the main potential confounder here; a pooled comparison alone could give the wrong direction or significance.
text: Serum albumin was measured by each hospital site's own laboratory (SITE column). Between-lab calibration or assay differences (e.g. bromocresol green vs purple), combined with differences in the TP53-mutant fraction across sites, can create, hide or reverse a pooled mutant-vs-wild-type albumin difference (Simpson's paradox). Tabulate TP53 status by SITE and mean albumin by SITE, and compare the pooled difference with within-site differences. If they disagree, base the conclusion on a site-adjusted or site-stratified estimate (e.g. albumin ~ TP53 + SITE, or site-centred albumin) rather than a pooled t-test.

reason: Misclassification of the exposure can dilute or distort the group comparison.
text: TP53_STATUS may disagree with TP53_VAF (some rows show status mutant with VAF 0.000). Cross-tabulate TP53_STATUS against TP53_VAF>0, count mutant-with-VAF-0 and wild-type-with-VAF>0, and check whether discordant cases cluster by SITE or batch. If discordance exists, run the analysis both with status as given and with the discordant cases corrected or excluded, and report whether the conclusion holds.

reason: A few bad values or a unit mismatch at one site can drive a mean difference on their own.
text: Check SERUM_ALBUMIN for implausible or sentinel values (0, negative, 999-type codes, values above ~6 g/dL) and for a site reporting in g/L rather than g/dL (about 10x the others). Summarise the albumin range per SITE. If found, convert units or exclude invalid values, then confirm the result with a robust method (Mann-Whitney or regression with site).

reason: This separates a TP53 effect from a general effect of sicker patients without over-adjusting.
text: Albumin is lower with worse performance status (ECOG_PS), low BMI/cachexia, older AGE and kidney dysfunction (SERUM_CREATININE). Compare these between TP53 groups. Report crude and adjusted estimates (e.g. albumin ~ TP53 + SITE + AGE, with ECOG and BMI added as a sensitivity analysis). Note that ECOG and BMI may be mediators, so adjusting for them is a sensitivity check, not the main model.

reason: Pseudoreplication inflates n and over-weights some patients, which can produce false significance.
text: Statin use is recorded per patient, but stromal score is per sample, and a patient may have several samples (e.g. primary and metastasis). Count samples per PATIENT_ID and tabulate SAMPLE_TYPE. If patients have more than one sample, do not treat samples as independent: use one sample per patient (preferably the primary tumour), aggregate per patient, or fit a mixed model with a patient random effect. Check whether the result holds in primary-only samples.

reason: This ties the label to an estimate and its uncertainty rather than to a p-value alone.
text: Both variables (TP53 status and serum albumin) exist, so the question can be tested. For the main (site-adjusted) model, report the direction and size of the mutant-minus-wild-type albumin difference in g/dL with a 95% CI and p-value. A non-significant result is not by itself proof of no difference. Weigh whether the evidence supports a lower albumin in mutants, contradicts it (an opposite-direction effect, or a precise null with a tight CI), or is inconclusive, and explain this in the reasoning.

reason: Exposure and outcome are in different tables, so a bad join silently corrupts the comparison.
text: Before merging the patient, sample and supplement tables, check that PATIENT_ID is unique in the patient and supplement tables. Count unmatched IDs on each side and confirm the row count after the merge. Settle any duplicate patient rows first, report how many samples were dropped, and never let a many-to-many join inflate n.

reason: Misclassified exposure can bias the group comparison toward or away from the null.
text: Check how the exposure is coded. STATIN_USE should be only 0/1, and STATIN_DOSE_MG should be >0 exactly when STATIN_USE=1. Look for missing or sentinel values. Handle contradictory records (e.g. a user with dose 0) explicitly, report how many there are, and run a sensitivity analysis. A dose-versus-score check can strengthen or weaken the interpretation.

reason: Sentinel values or outliers can flip or create an apparent group difference.
text: Look at the STROMAL_SCORE distribution in each group for skew, outliers and impossible or sentinel values (e.g. -999, NA codes). Remove or recode sentinels. Run a rank-based test (Mann-Whitney) or another robust check alongside any t-test, and base the conclusion on the direction and size of the effect rather than on a p-value driven by a few points.

reason: Technical batch effects can create or hide a crude difference between groups.
text: Processing batch may be confounded with statin group. After joining, cross-tabulate PROCESSING_BATCH by STATIN_USE and compare stromal score by batch. If batches differ in both score level and statin prevalence, adjust for batch (fixed effect) or compare within batch. A batch that is almost entirely one group gives no information on the effect. Avoid batch-correction methods that could remove the statin signal when the design is unbalanced.

QUESTION: What are the standard practices for handling processing-batch effects in gene expression signature scores when batch is partially associated with the group of interest (covariate adjustment, ComBat-style correction, or within-batch comparison), and what are the known pitfalls of each? ANSWER: NOT SETTLED BY WEB: the gateway failed (HTTP 403), so no page was read. From background knowledge only: the preferred approach is to put batch as a covariate in the outcome model (score ~ ER + batch), or to compare within batch and combine the strata. Pitfalls: (1) Correcting with ComBat or similar before testing, without group in the model, can remove real group signal. With group in the model, an unbalanced design gives overconfident, inflated significance and extra false positives (Nygaard, Rødland & Hovig 2016, Biostatistics). (2) Covariate adjustment cannot separate batch from group when they are fully confounded, and it loses precision when they are strongly associated. (3) Within-batch comparison loses power and excludes batches that hold only one group. If the ER effect keeps its direction but loses significance after adjustment, that points to lost precision or partial confounding, not to a reversal. Always cross-tabulate batch by group first (Leek et al. 2010, Nat Rev Genet). HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

text: FINDING: Haemoglobin is reported as g/dL (US, UK and most of the world), g/L (Canada, Australia, much of Europe and SI labs) or mmol/L (Netherlands and some Scandinavian labs, on a per-haem/Fe monomer basis). Conversions: g/L = g/dL x 10; mmol/L = g/dL x 0.6206 (g/dL = mmol/L x 1.611). Typical adult ranges: about 12-17.5 g/dL = 120-175 g/L = 7.4-10.9 mmol/L. In a single numeric column the three units form separate clusters (~7-11, ~12-17, ~120-175), so you can spot a site using a different unit by plotting per-site distributions. A site fixed effect will not fix this, because the difference is multiplicative; rescale to g/dL first. QUESTION: Alternative haemoglobin units, conversion factors and typical ranges in multicentre data. From background knowledge: a second, unrelated signature measured in the same batches serves as a negative-control outcome (as in RUV, Gagnon-Bartsch & Speed 2012, and Lipsitch et al. 2010). It should not differ by ER biologically, so if it differs across batches with roughly the same pattern as hypoxia, that points to a technical batch effect. If it does not vary by batch, or its ER difference vanishes within batch, the batch-hypoxia link is more likely biology or ER imbalance. In practice, regress the control score on batch (and on ER plus batch) and look for batch shifts. Batch effects shared with the control can then be removed by adjusting for batch or for the control score. This is only valid if the control is truly unrelated to ER. QUESTION: How is an unrelated signature in the same batches used as a negative control for batch effects? SOURCE: none retrieved (gateway down).

From background knowledge (Lakens 2017 equivalence testing, TOST): a null estimate counts as evidence against a directional hypothesis only when a smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) is set in advance and the CI excludes it. For 'ER+ lower', that means the upper end of the 90% CI (one-sided 95%) for ER+ minus ER- lies above -SESOI, so any decrease is smaller than meaningful, or the CI lies wholly in the opposite direction. If the CI includes both zero and -SESOI, the result is inconclusive ('cannot settle' in statistical terms). For signature z-scores a SESOI of about 0.2 SD (a small Cohen's d) is a common default. question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: How is an equivalence or non-inferiority test (e.g. two one-sided tests) used to argue that a non-significant difference rules out a clinically meaningful effect, and what margins are conventionally used for differences in haemoglobin (g/dL)? ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the research gateway returned HTTP 502 (Exa 403) on every search and contents call, so this answer comes from background knowledge. TOST: you pre-specify a margin delta and test H0: diff <= -delta and H0: diff >= +delta, each one-sided at alpha=0.05. Equivalence is concluded when the 90% CI lies entirely within (-delta, +delta). For the directional hypothesis (RT lowers Hb), a one-sided non-inferiority test fits better: the null 'RT lowers Hb by at least delta' is rejected when the lower CI bound of (RT minus no-RT) is above -delta. A non-significant p-value on its own does not show absence of an effect. No universal Hb margin exists. About 0.5 g/dL (sometimes 1.0 g/dL) is commonly used as a non-inferiority margin in anaemia/ESA/iron trials, and a difference of about 1 g/dL is generally treated as clinically meaningful. A null result supports 'False' only if the CI lower bound is above about -0.5 g/dL (or at least -1 g/dL). HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: What are the standard sex-specific haemoglobin thresholds for anaemia in adults, and how does chronic kidney disease or reduced renal function (serum creatinine) affect haemoglobin levels? ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED (gateway down). WHO: anaemia is Hb <13.0 g/dL in adult men and <12.0 g/dL in non-pregnant women (<11.0 g/dL in pregnancy); KDIGO 2012 uses the same cut-offs in CKD. Reduced renal function lowers Hb, mainly through reduced erythropoietin production, with iron deficiency, inflammation and shortened red-cell survival also contributing. Anaemia becomes more common as eGFR falls below ~60 mL/min/1.73m2 and is common below ~30. Higher serum creatinine is therefore plausibly linked to lower Hb. It confounds the RT–Hb comparison only if it is a pre-exposure difference between groups; if RT or nephrotoxic treatment affects the kidney, it may be a mediator, so adjust for it as a sensitivity analysis rather than in the primary model. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

text: FINDING: Duplicate patient records with different IDs are normally found by record linkage: deterministic (exact match on a set of fields) or probabilistic (Fellegi-Sunter weighting) matching on demographics and measurements. Two distinct patients matching exactly on several continuous lab values (e.g. glucose, creatinine, BMI recorded to a decimal place) is extremely unlikely by chance, roughly the product of the small per-variable match probabilities. So rows identical in content but with different IDs should be treated as likely duplicates, removed, and checked in a sensitivity analysis. Confidence medium; the web tool failed (HTTP 403) and no page was read. QUESTION: methods for detecting duplicate records with different identifiers, and how likely a chance exact match is. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_linkage (not fetched, tool failure).

Under this task's labels, Not verifiable is reserved for missing variables, so a non-significant same-direction result most plausibly maps to 'does not support', i.e. False rather than True. QUESTION: When comparing a gene-expression signature score between two genotype groups in bulk tumour data, what is the accepted practice for using a second, unrelated signature from the same assay as a negative control for technical or pre-analytical artefacts? ANSWER: The web did not settle this: all 3 research calls failed with HTTP 403, so no page was read. From general knowledge, unverified: treat it as a negative-control outcome (Lipsitch et al. 2010). Score a signature from the same assay that should not depend on TP53 and run the same comparison and model (same covariates, e.g. batch, site, purity, sample type). If the control differs between groups by a similar standardized effect, the hypoxia difference is likely an assay-wide technical or pre-analytical artefact. If the control is null while hypoxia differs, that supports specificity but does not prove it. Ischaemia/handling time selectively induces hypoxia genes, so you still need to adjust for site/batch. Random-signature work (Venet et al. 2011) shows that unrelated signatures often show associations, which is the reason specificity checks are needed. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

text: FINDING: Not settled from the web - all 4 research gateway calls failed (HTTP 502/Exa 403), so no page was read. Unverified background only: purity is commonly adjusted as a covariate in bulk-expression immune analyses (e.g. Aran et al. 2015), but in causal-inference terms adjusting for a variable on the causal path (ER status -> tumour composition/purity -> bulk IFNG score) estimates a direct effect, not the total effect, and can bias the group comparison (overadjustment bias, Schisterman et al. 2009); purity is downstream of ER biology rather than a technical confounder, unlike processing batch. Analysts should report the batch-adjusted estimate both with and without purity and label by whether the direction agrees. QUESTION: Is tumour purity a standard covariate or a mediator whose adjustment biases the ER-group effect on an IFN-gamma signature score? question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: When comparing a gene-expression signature score between two clinical groups that are unevenly distributed across processing batches, is it standard to adjust for tumour purity as a covariate, or is purity sometimes treated as a mediator whose adjustment biases the group effect? ANSWER: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB: all 4 research calls (2 search, 1 contents, 1 retry) failed with HTTP 502 (Exa 403), so I read no pages. Unverified background knowledge only: adjusting bulk immune scores for purity is common practice (Aran et al. 2015). In causal terms, though, purity can lie on the path ER status -> tumour/stroma/immune composition -> bulk IFNG score. If it does, adjusting for it gives a controlled direct effect rather than the total group effect and can bias the estimate (overadjustment bias, Schisterman et al. 2009). Processing batch is a true technical confounder; purity is arguably not. Recommendation: make the batch-adjusted model without purity the primary total-effect estimate, report the model with purity as a sensitivity analysis, and treat a small residual effect that appears or disappears only with purity adjustment as fragile. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.
